messages.author: c2585c52e059b919
messages.subject: Stan_Trace Question with random numbers of parameters.
parts:
Hi, All,

I hope you all have a wonderful holiday!

I have a parameter called theta with a length of 2000, namely theta[1] - thata[2000], and I want to check the Stan_Trace to check whether the parameter is converged. But I do not want to see all of them. So, I want to generate small amount of numbers of thetas randomly, say 20, and plot the trace.

I'm using the sample() function to generate 20 integers but I do not know how to use those numbers in the stan_trace functions. Any idea?

a <- sort(sample(0:2000, 20, replace = FALSE))
stan_trace(fit_m0, par=c("theta")

Thanks!

Sincerely,
Jiaqi

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Stan_Trace Question with random numbers of parameters.
parts:
Here's an example using one of the Stan demo models: 

fit <- stan_demo("eight_schools")
sel <- sort(sample(1:8, 3, replace = FALSE)) # pick random 3 of the 8 thetas
thetas_to_plot <- paste0("theta[", sel, "]")
stan_trace(fit, pars = thetas_to_plot)

Hope that helps, 

Jonah
